The map's name, in 1783 and 1800, for the kingdoms of the highlands west of Lake Victoria, in what are now Rwanda, Burundi, north-western Tanzania and south-western Uganda. The land lies along the Western Rift Valley, hence the label. The best known are Rwanda, Burundi and Karagwe, with the Haya kingdoms by the lake and Nkore to the north.

These were well-peopled states of banana and grain farmers and cattle owners, ruled by kings from courts that often moved. Cattle were the measure of wealth and rank. In Rwanda and Burundi the line between mostly herding Tutsi and mostly farming Hutu became a social ranking, which colonial rulers later made rigid, with terrible results in the genocide of 1994.

In these years Rwanda was growing by conquest. The older rivals Buganda and Bunyoro lay further north.
